philosophy.title: Pedagogical Philosophy & Educational Vision
philosophy.summary: Bridging abstract biological concepts with hands-on computational execution. Equipping life scientists with command-line proficiency, reproducible workflows, and rigorous algorithmic reasoning as core competencies for modern genomics.

pillars.title: Hands-On, Terminal-First Learning
pillars.description: Pairing computational lectures with real-world biological datasets, teaching students to work directly in Linux, Python, and R environments.

pillars.title: Reproducibility as a Core Standard
pillars.description: Instilling best practices in version control (Git), containerization, and reproducible bioinformatics workflows from the outset.

pillars.title: Individualized Mentorship & Ownership
pillars.description: Guiding undergraduate and graduate students to master analytical pipelines, formulate hypotheses, interpret multi-omics data, and communicate findings.

curriculumDevelopment.title: ICAR 5th Dean Committee Curriculum Revision
curriculumDevelopment.description: Designed 8 courses for the Bioinformatics module in B. Tech Biotechnology Degree under Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) 5th Dean committee for national course revision.

courses.title: Bioinformatics and Big Data Mining
courses.description: Advanced computational methods for biological big data: high-throughput sequencing analysis, sequence alignment algorithms, structural modeling, machine learning in genomics, and high-performance computing cluster utilization.
topics: NGS Quality Control & Variant Calling Pipelines
Machine Learning Applications in Biological Data

courses.title: Bioinformatics Tools and Their Application in Agriculture
courses.description: Graduate curriculum covering biological databases, molecular phylogenetics, pairwise and multiple sequence alignment, protein secondary structure prediction, and applied crop genomics.
topics: Biological Data Mining & NCBI / Ensembl E-utilities
Molecular Marker Discovery (SSRs and SNPs in Plant Breeding)

courses.title: Advances in Bioinformatics
courses.description: Doctoral curriculum on computational frontiers: comparative genomics, transcriptomic differential expression modeling, protein-protein interaction networks, and structural docking algorithms.
topics: Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) in Gene Prediction

courses.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics
courses.description: Foundational course establishing core computational competencies for undergraduate biotechnology majors, including Linux shell basics, sequence formats, and analytical servers.
topics: Biological Sequence Formats (FASTA, FASTQ, SAM/BAM, GFF3)
Primer Design & In Silico PCR Diagnostics

courses.title: Introduction to Genomics and Proteomics
courses.description: High-throughput technologies in genomics and proteomics: whole-genome sequencing, microarrays, mass spectrometry data analysis, and functional annotation of proteomes.
topics: Mass Spectrometry Peptide Identification & UniProt Proteomes

courses.title: Computational Biology
courses.description: Mathematical models in molecular biology, algorithm design for biological strings, population genetics modeling, and computational scripting.

courses.title: In-house Training
courses.description: Supervised hands-on research training and practical sessions for undergraduate biotechnology students in computational biology and bioinformatics tools.

workshops.title: NGS Data Analysis Workshop
workshops.audience: Graduate Students, Postdocs & Life Science Researchers
workshops.description: Hands-on training on RNA-Seq, ChIP-Seq, and variant calling pipelines.

workshops.title: Linux for Biologists
workshops.description: Command-line tools and scripting for biological data analysis.
workshops.stack: Bash • Linux Commands • Text Processing • Shell Scripting

workshops.title: Machine Learning in Bioinformatics
workshops.description: Python-based workshops on machine learning applications in biological data.
workshops.stack: Python • Scikit-Learn • Deep Learning • Sequence Models

mentoring.details: Mentor graduate students in bioinformatics methods and project design, developing computational algorithms for viral genome analysis and disease surveillance.
Mentored undergraduate and graduate researchers in machine learning pipelines for RNA-Seq, genome annotation, and variant analysis, and conducted workshops on NGS and Linux.
Assisted in teaching graduate and undergraduate courses in bioinformatics, genomics, and computational biology; supervised student research projects and laboratory sessions.
Taught undergraduate courses in bioinformatics and biotechnology, and supervised student research projects and internships.
